_instructions.purpose: This file holds the REAL tier (structured numbers pulled by hand from AlphaSense/IR releases/filings) and the TRACKED tier (qualitative status notes). Nothing in this file is fetched automatically. Edit it directly and commit.
how_to_add_a_real_data_point: 1. Find the series under `real_series` by its key (e.g. 'gpi_new_vehicle_sss').
2. Append a new object to that series' `data` array: {"period": "2026Q2", "value": <number>, "source": "<where you got it>", "note": "<optional 1-line commentary>"}.
3. Use fiscal-quarter labels like '2026Q2' for `period` consistently within a series.
4. Update the series' `last_updated` field to today's date (YYYY-MM-DD).
5. If a series has no clean historical run available, leave `data` as an empty array and keep `status: "awaiting data"` rather than estimating or fabricating a number.
6. Never overwrite prior entries — this file is the full history, versioned in git.
how_to_add_an_oem_truck_delivery_data_po: The 'oem_truck_deliveries' series (Section 3) uses a STRICT explicit schema instead of freeform note text — every entry MUST have exactly these fields, in this order:

- `oem` (string — "Ford" for Ford's aggregate Trucks category; "Ford - F-Series" for the F-Series line alone; GM is reported per nameplate as "GM - Silverado" / "GM - Sierra" since GM Authority discloses each separately. Keep these exact strings consistent across entries so the UI can group/filter by OEM.)
- `truck_units` (number — total truck/pickup units delivered that quarter, as defined in `note`)

- `yoy_pct` (number or null — year-over-year % change if the source discloses one for this exact figure, OR if it can be cleanly derived by subtracting/dividing two totals already disclosed in that same source (as done for Ford Q1 2026 and GM Silverado Q1 2026); use null rather than estimating one from unrelated figures)
- `note` (string — 1-2 sentences of qualitative color: what exactly `truck_units` covers, incentive/backlog commentary, etc.)

- `source_quality` (string — 'primary' = you read the OEM's own table/release directly; 'primary-derived' = computed from two primary figures; 'relayed' = OEM's official table but content obtained second-hand (e.g. via a search index) because the document blocks automated access; 'secondary' = trade press only. The page shows a badge for each; 'relayed' and 'secondary' are flagged visibly.)

- BASIS RULE for GM: always use GM's TOTAL Silverado / TOTAL Sierra lines (Silverado includes medium duty and the EV; Sierra includes the EV), with the % change printed on that same line — never pair LD+HD units with a total-line YoY (that caused the Q1/Q2 errors fixed 2026-10-27).
Append new quarters as new objects to `data`; never overwrite prior entries. Update the series' `last_updated` to today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) whenever you add a row.
how_to_update_a_tracked_note: 1. Find the item under `tracked_notes` by its key (e.g. 'val_u_line').
2. Update `status` (short phrase) and `detail` (1-3 sentences) to reflect the latest known state.
4. Optionally append the prior status to `history` as {"date": ..., "status": ...} before overwriting, to keep a paper trail.
_instructions.data_honesty_rule: Every value in this file must trace to a specific report, filing, or call — cite it in `source`. If you don't have a real figure, leave the series/note empty with status 'awaiting data' rather than estimating.
how_to_add_a_used_market_month: Series `used_market_monthly` (Section 6). One object per month, STRICT fields: month ('YYYY-MM'), muvvi_index, muvvi_yoy_pct, wholesale_days_supply, retail_avg_listing_price, retail_listing_yoy_pct, retail_days_supply, retail_sales_pace_yoy_pct, note, source.

Wholesale fields come from Cox's Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index report (released ~5th business day of the following month); retail fields from Cox's used-vehicle inventory report (~mid-month, vAuto Live Market View).
Record values as FIRST reported; if Cox later revises, say so in `note`. Use null (never an estimate) when Cox gives only a vague phrase like 'up over 1%'.
Update the series' `last_updated` whenever you add a row. The page computes the retail-vs-wholesale spread (retail_listing_yoy_pct minus muvvi_yoy_pct) itself.
how_to_add_a_gpi_used_vehicle_quarter: Series `gpi_used_vehicle` (Section 8). One object per quarter from GPI's 8-K Ex. 99.1; fields listed in the series' `schema`.

us_* from the 'Reported Operating Data — U.S.' table; ss_* from Key Performance Metrics (same-store, consolidated); days' supply from 'Days' Supply in Inventory'; *_musd from the consolidated reported revenue / gross profit blocks (used = retail + wholesale).
GPI reports Q3 2026 on Oct 28, 2026 — add a 2026Q3 row from that release.
_instructions.optional_headline_field: Any `real_series` row may carry an optional `headline`: ONE line (<~170 chars) using only numbers already in that row's `note`. When a row's note is long (>260 chars) the page collapses the note behind a 'Show details' toggle and displays the `headline` above it, so the gist stays visible. Rows with short notes don't need one. OEM rows (Section 4) and the two used-vehicle tables don't use headlines.

gpi_ps_growth.label: GPI Parts & Service (P&S) Same-Store Growth
gpi_ps_growth.unit: % YoY, same-store customer-pay P&S revenue (best available proxy for the modeled 'P&S annuity' growth rate — see note for what is and isn't formally disclosed)
gpi_ps_growth.source_guidance: GPI Q2 2026 earnings call transcript (spoken remarks, not a formally tabled metric) + GPI Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, Key Performance Metrics table, which discloses P&S gross profit/margin but not a P&S revenue growth line)
gpi_ps_growth.status: populated (mixed: one directly-disclosed % + formally tabled GP/GM data + qualitative color)

data.source: GPI Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, July 30, 2026 (via Investing.com). https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-group-1-automotive-posts-q2-2026-miss-shares-sink-93CH-4825412
data.note: CFO Daniel McHenry, verbatim: "Same-store customer pay and warranty revenues increased approximately 4% and 1% respectively" (Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025). CEO Daryl Kenningham added this 4% customer-pay growth "lapped a 14% growth quarter last year, and it was 10% before the CDK impact" — i.e. a tough prior-year comp, not a clean run-rate read. Neither figure is a formally tabled same-store metric (unlike the NV same-store data in Section 7) — both are spoken remarks only. VS. THE 6%/4% ASSUMPTION: at +4% same-store customer-pay growth on a tough comp, the actual disclosed trend sits at or below the ~4% revised-down case, not the historical ~6% assumption. The formally tabled numbers reinforce this: consolidated same-store P&S gross profit was actually -0.2% YoY with same-store gross margin down 1.3pts (56.0% vs 57.3%), and consolidated REPORTED P&S gross profit was -3.4% YoY ($389.0M vs $402.8M) — so even the revenue-side +4% isn't converting to GP growth. Context: Q2 2025 had one-time same-store U.S. warranty revenue growth of ~32% (Tundra + GM engine recalls), inflating the comp base GPI is lapping this quarter — Kenningham: "Setting aside last year's one-time recall benefit, the underlying performance of the after-sales business remains resilient." RETENTION/COMPETITIVE COLOR (same call): vehicles bought during the low-volume 2020-2022 period are now reaching the end of factory warranty, "which is generally a high defection point" to independent/aftermarket service; Kenningham called the aftermarket "our real competition as franchise dealers," noting consumers have "more provider options, and they have more increased affordability pressures." GPI's response: a $17.76 oil-change promotion the company says "recaptured some at-risk customers that were going to the aftermarket," and a chain-wide rollout of "One Care," a discounted maintenance plan targeting 4-7 year-old-vehicle owners. Could not verify the 'underbenchmarking' comment on deals referenced in the request — searched the freely-accessible portions of the Q1 and Q2 2026 call transcripts (Investing.com, Motley Fool) and could not locate that specific term; omitting rather than guessing at its content. Source for the P&S GP/GM figures: GPI Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2026-07-30), Key Performance Metrics table. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001031203/000103120326000121/a2026q2exhibit991.htm
data.headline: Same-store customer-pay +4% (spoken, lapping a 14% comp) vs. the 6% / 4% assumptions: at or below the 4% case. Same-store P&S gross profit -0.2%, margin -1.3 pts.

CEO Daryl Kenningham, Q2 call, verbatim: "Persistent affordability challenges for the automotive consumer, challenges sourcing used vehicles, and short-term disruption from our largely completed corporate rebranding efforts combined to lower our new and used vehicle volumes." On days' supply: "We began the quarter with 26 days supply, and in some markets, we never really recovered from that low days supply." On restocking: "An easy solution would've been to restock by purchasing auction units. However, in our minds, that's not a great outcome given the potential gross profit impact that can have." Val-U-Line was not discussed in the verbatim portion of either call transcript. rebranding_seo.detail: GPI's Q2 2026 earnings release states the company "advanced our corporate rebranding to more than 60% completion." On the Q2 2026 earnings call, CEO Daryl Kenningham attributed roughly two-thirds of the quarter's ~5% same-store new-vehicle unit decline to transitional rebranding/organic-search effects, concentrated in Texas (~80% of GPI's Ford/GM business) as legacy store names (e.g. Sterling McCall, Advantage, Beck & Masten in Houston) are consolidated under the new brand. leverage_trajectory.status: 3.3x rent-adjusted leverage at June 30, 2026 (up from 2.7x a year earlier); expected to stay below 4x through Hennessy deal close, targeting return to target leverage by mid-to-late 2027
leverage_trajectory.detail: Per Q2 2026 earnings call commentary: rent-adjusted leverage ratio was 3.3x at June 30, 2026, up from 2.7x a year earlier due to acquisition activity (incl. the pending Hennessy Automobile Companies acquisition in Atlanta). Total debt was $3.36B (-9.1% YoY) and cash was $164.5M (up from $32.5M at YE2025). Management expects leverage to stay below 4x through the Hennessy close and to return to GPI's target leverage level by mid-to-late 2027, with Q3/Q4 disposition proceeds helping pay down acquisition-related debt. The user's brief cited '~4x currently' — the actual disclosed figure this quarter is 3.3x; flagging the discrepancy rather than silently overwriting either number.
